# sincospif

> Simultaneously compute the [sine][@stdlib/math/base/special/sinf] and [cosine][@stdlib/math/base/special/cosf] of a single-precision floating-point number times [π][@stdlib/constants/float32/pi].

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var sincospif = require( '@stdlib/math/base/special/sincospif' );
```

#### sincospif( x )

Simultaneously computes the [sine][@stdlib/math/base/special/sinf] and [cosine][@stdlib/math/base/special/cosf] of a single-precision floating-point number times [π][@stdlib/constants/float32/pi] more accurately than `sincosf(pi*x)`, especially for large `x`.

```javascript
var v = sincospif( 0.0 );
// returns <Float32Array>[ 0.0, 1.0 ]

v = sincospif( 0.5 );
// returns <Float32Array>[ 1.0, 0.0 ]

v = sincospif( 0.1 );
// returns <Float32Array>[ ~0.309, ~0.951 ]

v = sincospif( NaN );
// returns <Float32Array>[ NaN, NaN ]
```

#### sincospif.assign( x, out, stride, offset )

Simultaneously computes the [sine][@stdlib/math/base/special/sinf] and [cosine][@stdlib/math/base/special/cosf] of a single-precision floating-point number times [π][@stdlib/constants/float32/pi] more accurately than `sincosf(pi*x)`, especially for large `x`, and assigns results to a provided output array.

```javascript
var Float32Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float32' );

var out = new Float32Array( 2 );

var v = sincospif.assign( 0.0, out, 1, 0 );
// returns <Float32Array>[ 0.0, 1.0 ]

var bool = ( v === out );
// returns true
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var uniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/uniform' );
var sincospif = require( '@stdlib/math/base/special/sincospif' );

var opts = {
    'dtype': 'float32'
};
var x = uniform( 100, -100.0, 100.0, opts );

var y;
var i;
for ( i = 0; i < x.length; i++ ) {
    y = sincospif( x[ i ] );
    console.log( 'sincospif(%d) = [ %d, %d ]', x[ i ], y[ 0 ], y[ 1 ] );
}
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<!-- C usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

### Usage

```c
#include "stdlib/math/base/special/sincospif.h"
```

#### stdlib_base_sincospif( x, &sine, &cosine )

Simultaneously computes the [sine][@stdlib/math/base/special/sinf] and [cosine][@stdlib/math/base/special/cosf] of a single-precision floating-point number times [π][@stdlib/constants/float32/pi] more accurately than `sincosf(pi*x)`, especially for large `x`.

```c
float cosine;
float sine;

stdlib_base_sincospif( 4.0f, &sine, &cosine );
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **x**:      `[in] float` input value.
-   **sine**:   `[out] float*` destination for the sine.
-   **cosine**: `[out] float*` destination for the cosine.

```c
void stdlib_base_sincospif( const float x, float *sine, float *cosine );
```

</section>

<!-- C API usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

### Examples

```c
#include "stdlib/math/base/special/sincospif.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main( void ) {
    const float x[] = { 0.0f, 0.5f, 1.0f, 2.0f };

    float cosine;
    float sine;
    int i;
    for ( i = 0; i < 4; i++ ) {
        stdlib_base_sincospif( x[ i ], &sine, &cosine );
        printf( "x: %f => sine: %f, cosine: %f\n", x[ i ], sine, cosine );
    }
}
```

</section>
